brief: Meta's Muse agent, launched September 8, drove META from 14x to 21x forward earnings and up 27% to a $777.59 peak, with the sell-side pricing a $30tn consumer and $25tn enterprise opportunity. Hunterbrook Media, citing TickerTrends and disclosing a short position, then reported downloads down 21.1% from their September 24 peak and net daily user additions down 62.4% from the initial surge to about 74K a day, with engagement (app reviews) also falling. That slowdown lands just as Morgan Stanley's cost model, sized for 1 billion users, shows Muse costs $3-$130 per user per month to serve (base case $37, which Nowak calls a ceiling) against Meta's roughly $70 ARPU; at today's actual 1.8mn-2.7mn-user base the compute bill is a rounding error, Meta already has the CPUs for a billion users, and real ad-auction monetization isn't expected until "late '27/'28 at the earliest." Slower growth pushes that timeline out further and shifts negotiating leverage toward Amazon, which has blocked Muse from its store. Street price targets (Morgan Stanley $775, JPMorgan $920, BofA $810) sit well above the price regardless.
